feedback.goal: Move the reviewed HMR feature from its stacked runtime-generation parent onto the merged main branch without changing feature content or weakening its verification evidence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The HMR-only commits are replayed directly onto the merged runtime-generation main commit.
The rebased branch tree is byte-equivalent to the previously reviewed and published HMR head before this feedback record is added.
The prospective main-based comparison contains only the expected HMR feature surface rather than the already-merged runtime-generation patch.
The complete repository verification gate passes on the rebased tree.

outcome.summary: The HMR feature now has the merged runtime-generation commit on main as its direct base, retains the previously reviewed feature tree, and passes the complete repository gate.

what_worked: The merged runtime-generation tree exactly matched its reviewed source head, allowing the HMR-only commits to replay without conflicts.
A direct old-head versus rebased-head comparison proved behavior-bearing repository content was unchanged.
Comparing both two-dot and three-dot ranges against main produced the same bounded HMR feature surface after the rebase.
what_failed: Retargeting the pull request before rewriting squash-merge ancestry caused the hosting service to include the already-merged dependency in its comparison and report the branch as conflicting.
The earlier completion feedback references the pre-main-rebase commit identity and is therefore superseded by this record.

calls.name: pull-request-inspection
calls.purpose: Confirm the dependency merge and identify the inflated comparison caused by squash-merge ancestry.

calls.name: git-rebase
calls.purpose: Replay only the HMR commits onto the merged main commit.

calls.name: git-comparison
calls.purpose: Prove tree preservation and verify the prospective main-based change surface.

calls.name: pnpm-run-check
calls.purpose: Run the complete repository gate after the ancestry rewrite.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: The pull request base was changed before accounting for the dependency pull request's squash merge, briefly producing an inflated and conflicting hosted comparison.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: After a stacked dependency merges, inspect whether its source commit is an ancestor of the target base before retargeting the dependent pull request.

evidence.summary: The dependency pull request merged runtime-generation attestation into main with a content-equivalent squash commit.
The reviewed HMR commit series was replayed directly onto the merged main commit without conflicts.
The rebased head and the previously published reviewed head had no file-content differences.
Two-dot and three-dot comparisons against merged main agreed on the same 37-file HMR feature surface.
Typecheck, build, 34 test files with 219 passing tests and 7 opt-in skips, capsule validation, policy verification, core evaluation, and benchmark evaluation all passed without a hard stop.

uncertainty.statement: The hosting service has not yet recomputed pull request mergeability for the rebased commit because publication remains approval-gated.
uncertainty.resolution: After exact external-write approval, publish the rebased head and confirm the pull request reports the intended base, bounded diff, successful CI, and clean mergeability.

uncertainty.statement: HMR recorder attribution has no independently persisted admission receipt and therefore is not an authorization source.
uncertainty.resolution: Add a separately designed receipt and verifier only when a future automated consumer needs authenticated HMR admission evidence.

notes: The repository owner reported that dependency pull request 5 merged, activating the previously agreed retargeting step.
Final maintainer review remains pending in pull request 6.
Publishing the rebased head requires a new exact external-write approval bound to its final commit.
